name: dodge_viper_84_v10
label: Dodge Viper 8.4 L V10 (pushrod, odd-firing 90°/54°)
based_on: Dodge / SRT Viper 8.4 L V10 (Gen V, 2013-2017)

sources.what: Chrysler Group (now Stellantis) press release on the 2013 SRT Viper V10. Manufacturer; bore, stroke, rod length, valve sizes, compression, redline.
Chrysler press release for the 2008 Dodge Viper SRT10 (first 8.4). Manufacturer; intake, heads, VVT description.
supercars.net page for the 2008 Viper SRT-10: reproduces the Chrysler release plus a spec table.
English Wikipedia Viper engine page; displacement and peak rpm figures.
rerev.com firing-order page for the Dodge 8.4 L; automotive reference site, not a factory source.
English Wikipedia V10 engine page; states the Viper is a 90-degree odd-firing engine.
English Wikipedia Firing order page; lists the Viper V10 among odd-firing engines.
Audi MediaCenter engine text for the R8 V10; used only as the stated 54/90 interval for a 90-degree shared-pin V10.

notes: Sourced: bore, stroke, rod length, compression, valve diameters (one intake, one exhaust valve), 6200 rpm redline, headers with one runner per cylinder on each bank, side exhausts. Firing order 1-10-9-4-3-6-5-8-7-2 with odd cylinders on the left bank is from a firing-order reference site, not a Chrysler document. The 90/54-degree intervals and the five shared crank pins are a well-supported inference, not a quoted Viper fact: Wikipedia calls the engine odd-firing, and Audi states 54/90 for its own 90-degree shared-pin V10. Estimated, not sourced: valve lift, cam timing and duration (the real exhaust lobes are phased by a cam-in-cam system; one fixed timing is used), intake runner and throttle sizes (the engine has two throttle bodies; one of equivalent default size is used), exhaust primary and pipe sizes, no cross-over between the two side pipes, idle speed. Left to the simulator's defaults: plenum and airbox, collector volume, muffler, flywheel inertia. Also estimates: friction_scale, heat_q, burn_scale (the simulator's friction, heat-release and burn-rate scales), set with the other estimated fields so that simulated torque and power come near the published figures; no sourced number was changed.

vehicle.name: SRT Viper coupe (2013)
vehicle.notes: Base SRT Viper (not GTS, no Track Package), Tremec TR6060 six-speed manual. All figures are from Chrysler's 2013 specification sheet and press release. wheel_radius_m is from the sheet's 764 revolutions per mile for the rear tyre (my conversion), so it is a published rolling radius. Top speed 206 mph converted to km/h.
